paragraphs: It's the first day of the holiday games. The sun is hot, and the grass is green. Teacher Kim has a game for the children. "We have a hop game," she says. Twenty children stand in a line. Mia is first, and Lily is third. Ben is sixth. Leo is twentieth, the last child in the line. Leo says, "I'm always last!" Tom films the game with his phone. He stands next to the net.

"One, two, three, hop!" says Teacher Kim. The children hop on one leg. Mia is quick, and she hops to the end first. Ben comes second. Lily comes fourth. Leo hops very, very slowly. He wears funny red socks, and they fall down. He hops and laughs and hops again. At the end, Teacher Kim says, "Leo is eleventh!"

"Eleventh! That's my best!" says Leo. "Do you want to see the film?" asks Tom. Tom shows him the film. Leo looks at his funny red socks and laughs. After the game, the children play football. Leo kicks the ball, and it goes into the net. It's a goal! "That's my first goal!" he shouts. Now Leo isn't last. He is the first to score for his friends. They clap and shout, "Well done, Leo!"
text.summary: At the holiday games, twenty children hop in a line. Leo is always last, but this time he does well, and he scores a goal after the game.
